text:
alyssa: Quick proposal — build a tiny package-concierge CLI that operators run on bastions for air-gapped upgrades. It mediates between operator media (USB/NFS) or a one-way mirror and the node-local seed-agent. Goals: low friction, offline-first security, resumable transfers, and clear audit artifacts.

ben: Sounds promising. Is this meant to replace seed-agent or complement it?

alyssa: Complement. seed-agent remains the on-node enforcer for activation semantics. concierge is ephemeral, UX-focused, never holds signing keys; it only verifies signed manifests and streams blobs to seed-agent.

carlos: Main worry: metadata leakage. concierge must not phone home. Default should be fully offline unless operator explicitly enables mirror fetch.

diana: Agreed. Two modes: offline-ingest (no outbound) and mirror-proxy (operator-provided mirror URL; outbound allowed only for concierge). Telemetry off by default; opt-in via explicit flag/env.

alyssa: Proposed end-to-end flow: 1) concierge validates manifest sig locally using operator trust roots; 2) concierge streams content chunked & resumable to seed-agent over mTLS; 3) seed-agent stages chunks, verifies checksums + sigs, assigns monotonic manifest id; 4) operator triggers seed-agent activate --manifest-id X which runs activation window and atomically flips activation pointer if checks pass.

ben: How do we avoid partial activations on transfer failure?

carlos: seed-agent staging + atomic pointer swap. Provide an apply-token that concierge requests so resumed uploads tie to the staging record. If activate fails, rollback is simply switching back to previous pointer.

alyssa: CLI sketches: 
redwood-concierge ingest --source /mnt/usb --manifest /mnt/usb/redwood.json --target 10.0.0.5:8443 --verify
redwood-concierge resume --token abc123 --target 10.0.0.5:8443
redwood-concierge mirror --manifest https://mirror.local/redwood.json --allow-outbound --target 10.0.0.5:8443
redwood-concierge dry-run --manifest /mnt/usb/redwood.json

diana: Security model: concierge runs as operator user; seed-agent runs as system service. Require one-time registration token (displayed on admin console) to bind concierge to the node. Use mutual TLS with short-lived certs. Concierge must accept multiple trust roots and refuse ambiguous manifests.

carlos: Storage semantics: staging must be copy-on-write with reference counting. Keep previous image until activate completes. Rollback is activate --previous which repoints activation pointer after quick health checks.

ben: Failure modes: what if operator disconnects during activate? seed-agent should use an activation lease. After lease expiry the system can auto-rollback or require manual reconciliation. Also provide operator-signed audit record JSON that concierge writes and seed-agent stores.

alyssa: Performance knobs: conservative defaults — parallel fetch up to 4, dedupe enabled. Provide --unsafe-fast for aggressive parallelism and --dry-run for approvals. Add --simulate-fail-after N for CI.

infra-bot: TODO: add unit tests for resume and integration test for concierge --simulate-fail-after N-chunks to exercise idempotency.

open-questions: registration UX (token vs QR vs one-time file); chunking policy (fixed 4MB vs adaptive based on RTT/bandwidth); whether concierge should auto re-stream from mirror after failed staging or require explicit resume.

diana: My votes: token + QR for convenience; adaptive chunking based on latency; allow re-stream only after seed-agent signals resume-allowed.

ben: +1 adaptive chunking; add a perf-mode toggle.

carlos: +1 token/QR; keep logs verbose by default and ensure dry-run exists for approvals.

alyssa: I'll draft a short RFC with diagrams, syscall-level notes (umask, secure tmpdir, chroot option), and a diagnostic mode for verbose logs to include in support bundles. Will link RFC in #architecture and tag reviewers once ready. :thumbsup:
